sequence_strategy: Mr. Castillo asked us, so Email 1 answers his request in his own terms (three 24/7 Atacama lithium sites, costly and hazardous contracted crews, Anglo American referral, Q3 budget) and leads with the strongest verified proof: SQM's own published FlytBase deployment in northern Chile [S1]. Each follow-up then adds one new useful item tied to a different MEDDPICC gap: Atacama operating conditions and SQM's move to 24/7 dock surveillance (Decision Criteria), a forwardable five-bullet summary for his safety, IT and procurement colleagues (Paper Process), and a close-the-loop note that offers to hold until his Q3 budget conversation (Champion). Asks get smaller as the thread goes quiet, from a call with two slots to a yes/no on timing.

tone_adaptation.seniority: Head of Operations, Northern Operations Division: peer-level, brief and understated, formal 'Dear Mr. Castillo' throughout, outcomes and crew safety before any product detail, no pressure for a quick close.
tone_adaptation.industry: Mining: language is about crews, field exposure, remote sites and round-the-clock operations; acronyms spelled out; the proof point is a mining deployment in the same desert (SQM iodine, 678 km2) [S1], and Email 2 uses site conditions at about 2,300 m with strong temperature swings [S25] and SQM's own order of extra docks for 24/7 surveillance [S1].
tone_adaptation.stated_context: Mirrors every fact he gave (3 large-scale 24/7 lithium sites, Atacama, contracted crews expensive and hazardous, referred by Anglo American, Q3 budget conversation). Because SQM already runs FlytBase in iodine [S1], Email 1 asks how his sites relate to that programme rather than assuming they are the same. The referral is acknowledged but no claim is made about the Anglo American relationship, since the kept research does not verify one. Times are in America/Santiago and a Spanish offer is included for a Chilean buyer.

emails.send_when: Friday 6 November 2026, within 1 hour of the inbound (same business hour, Santiago time)
emails.goal: Confirm we understood his request, show the closest proof (SQM's own deployment), open the two most important gaps and book a 30-minute call with the AE.
emails.subject: Re: Autonomous inspection for our Atacama lithium sites
emails.body:
Dear Mr. Castillo,

Thank you for your note, and for the referral from Anglo American. You are looking for drone-based inspection across three large-scale, 24/7 lithium sites in the Atacama, so that you rely less on contracted crews that are expensive and hazardous, ahead of your Q3 budget conversation.

Docked drones flying scheduled missions at each site can reduce how often people go into the field, and give your Q3 discussion measured results rather than estimates.

Your own company is the closest reference. FlytBase's published case study describes SQM's iodine operation across 678 km2 in northern Chile running two autonomous dock missions a day, which doubled inspection frequency with more than 95% mission reliability.

Two questions to prepare:
1. How do your three sites relate to that programme, and how often do contracted crews inspect them today?
2. Besides yourself, who will take part in the Q3 budget conversation?

Would Wednesday 11 November at 11:00 or Thursday 12 November at 15:00, Santiago time, suit a 30-minute call? You are welcome to bring a safety or IT colleague.

Con gusto podemos continuar en español.

Kind regards,
Samruddhi Sontakke
Business Development, FlytBase
emails.why_this_email_now: He asked us directly and the lead is P1, so a specific reply within the business hour matters more than anything else. Mirroring his own words earns agreement, and the SQM case [S1] is proof from inside his own company and desert.
emails.why_next: If he does not reply, Email 2 adds something he would miss: what Atacama conditions and 24/7 operation mean for an autonomous system, and asks his Decision Criteria.
emails.success_signal: He accepts a slot, says how his sites relate to the iodine programme, or names who joins the Q3 conversation.

emails.send_when: Tuesday 10 November 2026, 10:30 Santiago time (+2 business days), same thread
emails.goal: Add one useful point on operating conditions and learn what a system must prove at his sites.
emails.subject: Re: Autonomous inspection for our Atacama lithium sites
emails.body:
Dear Mr. Castillo,

One point on Atacama conditions. Chile's labour authority describes SQM Salar at about 2,300 metres, with strong temperature swings for outdoor workers. The same FlytBase case study notes that SQM's security department has ordered additional docks to run 24/7 surveillance, which is close to your round-the-clock requirement.

What would a system need to prove at your sites, for example heat, dust, wind or night operation, before you trusted it around the clock?

Wednesday 11:00 or Thursday 15:00 Santiago time remain open for a 30-minute call.

Kind regards,
Samruddhi Sontakke
Business Development, FlytBase
emails.why_this_email_now: Two business days is enough for a senior buyer to have read Email 1. A new, relevant fact about his operating environment and a 24/7 use inside SQM is more useful than a reminder.
emails.why_next: Email 3 shifts from him to his colleagues: a forwardable summary for safety, IT and procurement, and the Paper Process question.
emails.success_signal: He lists technical criteria (heat, dust, altitude, night flights, integration) or accepts a slot.

emails.send_when: Tuesday 17 November 2026, 11:00 Santiago time (about +7 business days), same thread
emails.goal: Equip him to share the idea internally and learn how SQM buys this kind of technology.
emails.subject: Re: Autonomous inspection for our Atacama lithium sites
emails.body:
Dear Mr. Castillo,

In case it helps, here is a summary you can forward to safety, IT or procurement:
- Problem: contracted inspection crews at three 24/7 Atacama sites are costly and exposed.
- Approach: docked drones fly scheduled RGB and thermal missions.
- Safety: fewer routine trips into hazardous areas.
- IT: SQM's iodine programme already sends drone data to its Azure environment.
- Next step: scope one site before Q3.

Does SQM usually buy technology like this directly or through a local integrator?

Kind regards,
Samruddhi Sontakke
Business Development, FlytBase
emails.why_this_email_now: Enterprise mining purchases involve operations, safety, IT and supply chain. By touch 3 the playbook calls for a forwardable summary so he can act as our champion without extra work.
emails.why_next: Email 4 closes the loop politely and offers to hold until his Q3 budget conversation, while checking who leads this internally.
emails.success_signal: He forwards the summary, names a procurement route (direct or integrator), or copies a colleague.

emails.send_when: Wednesday 25 November 2026, 11:00 Santiago time (about +13 business days), same thread
emails.goal: Close the loop without pressure, offer to hold until Q3 and confirm who leads this.

emails.why_this_email_now: After three useful touches with no reply, more emails would cost goodwill. A clear, no-guilt close respects a senior Chilean buyer and ties the next contact to his own Q3 timeline.
emails.why_next: End of the active sequence. The lead moves to value nurture every 4-6 weeks (case study, implementation approach, objections, scoped pilot) with one refreshed touch before his Q3 budget conversation.
emails.success_signal: He gives a check-back date, names the internal lead, or replies that the timing is now right.
